Sukarno’s speech at the 1955 Bandung Conference was a key moment for Asian and African nations, many of which had recently gained or were seeking independence from colonial powers.  
He emphasizes that without peace, “our independence means little” and “our revolutions will not be allowed to run their course.”  
The context of the Bandung Conference was about promoting Afro-Asian solidarity against colonialism and neocolonialism, not primarily communism, gender equality, or environmental issues.  
Thus, the “revolutions” refer to the struggles for decolonization and national independence.
